difficulty_reason: For a continuous map of weakly admissible topological rings, the lemma states that tautness is equivalent to the condition that the closures of the extensions of the weak ideals of definition are weak ideals of definition forming a fundamental system (statement lines 1318-1326). One direction is read off from the remarks following the definition of tautness (proof lines 1328-1330). For the other, the proof takes a weak ideal of definition of the source, uses tautness to see that the closure of its extension is open, and then uses the statement that the set of topologically nilpotent elements is a closed ideal to show that this closure consists of topologically nilpotent elements, hence is a weak ideal of definition; tautness also gives that these closures form a fundamental system of open ideals, which completes the verification (proof lines 1330-1339). The claim is H2: the non-trivial direction is proved by combining openness from tautness with the description of the topologically nilpotent elements, and both halves of the conclusion are established.
